title: Mycosynthesis of silver nanoparticles and their characterization
author: Madakka, Jayaraju, et al.
materials: Analytical grade chemicals were used in the current study. Silver nitrate (Ag NO3) be procure from Sigma-Aldrich Chemicals (USA). Fungal and bacterial growth medium were procured from Oxoid Company (UK). The three test bacteria used for the antimicrobial study were procured from the Microbial Type Culture Collection (MTCC) (India).

steps.title: Collect reagents and media
steps.instruction: Obtain analytical‑grade silver nitrate (AgNO₃) from Sigma‑Aldrich (USA), fungal and bacterial growth media from Oxoid (UK), and the three test bacterial strains from the Microbial Type Culture Collection (MTCC, India) for use in the extracellular synthesis of silver nanoparticles.

steps.title: Extracellular synthesis of AgNPs
steps.instruction: Incubate the fungal strains Fusarium semitectum and Aspergillus niger under appropriate growth conditions, collect the aqueous filtrates, and add silver nitrate to each filtrate to allow enzymatic reduction of Ag⁺ ions to stable extracellular silver nanoparticles.

steps.title: Monitor nanoparticle formation by UV‑vis
steps.instruction: Record the UV‑visible spectrum of each reaction mixture. Observe a surface plasmon resonance (SPR) band at 420 nm for Fusarium semitectum‑derived AgNPs and at 450 nm for Aspergillus niger‑derived AgNPs. A strong peak at 440 nm is also seen for the cell deposit mixed with AgNO₃. Note that after 3 days of incubation the SPR intensity no longer increases, indicating complete reduction of silver ions.
